story: Sri Dhanvanthri Ayurveda is named after Lord Dhanvanthri, honoured in the Indian tradition as the physician of the gods and the source of Ayurveda.
We combine consultation, traditional therapies such as Panchakarma and Varma, yoga guidance and a herbal pharmacy that prepares the Narmadha range under one roof.
Because Ayurveda is personal, we begin every relationship with a conversation. The doctor reviews your history, your daily routine and your goals before suggesting anything.

ayurveda.lead: Ayurveda is a traditional system of health that originated in the Indian subcontinent thousands of years ago.

sections.heading: The three doshas
sections.body: Ayurveda describes three basic constitutions or doshas: Vata, Pitta and Kapha. Traditionally, health is seen as a balance among them, shaped by diet, sleep, season, stress and habits.

sections.heading: How a practitioner assesses you
sections.body: A practitioner may ask about your history, digestion, sleep and daily routine, observe the pulse and the body's signs, and then suggest diet and lifestyle changes, therapies or herbal preparations suited to you.

sections.heading: Food and routine
sections.body: Ayurveda gives great importance to eating according to your constitution, hunger and the season, to regular sleep, and to managing stress. Individual advice differs, so please ask the doctor rather than following general rules.

sections.heading: Choosing a practitioner
sections.body: Because many centres offer Ayurvedic services, we encourage you to consult only authorised Ayurvedic practitioners and to ask any centre about their qualifications and registration.

sections.heading: Branches of Ayurveda
sections.body: Classical Ayurveda describes eight branches, including general medicine (Kaya Chikitsa), surgery (Shalya), ear, nose, throat and eye care (Shalakya), paediatrics (Baala), psychiatry (Graha), toxicology (Agada), rejuvenation (Rasayana) and fertility (Vajikarana).

panchakarma.lead: Panchakarma, meaning five actions, is a traditional programme of cleansing and rejuvenation for the body and mind.
panchakarma.overview: In Ayurveda, Panchakarma is traditionally used to help the body let go of what it no longer needs and to prepare it for rest and rebuilding. It is planned individually and carried out under supervision.

steps.name: Vamana
steps.body: A supervised therapeutic procedure traditionally associated with balancing Kapha.

steps.name: Virechana
steps.body: A supervised cleansing of the digestive tract using medicines chosen by the doctor, traditionally associated with Pitta.

steps.name: Vasti (Niruha and Anuvasana)
steps.body: Herbal medicated enemas, traditionally associated with Vata.

steps.name: Nasya
steps.body: Medicated oils applied through the nose, traditionally used for the head and neck region.

steps.name: Raktamokshana
steps.body: Traditionally described as the fifth action; used only where the doctor judges it appropriate.

panchakarma.preparation: Panchakarma is usually preceded by oil massage (snehana) and sudation (swedana), with a light diet before and after. The doctor will explain what to expect and what to avoid.
benefits: Traditionally used to support relaxation and a sense of wellbeing
Often taken as part of a seasonal or routine wellness plan
Planned together with diet and lifestyle guidance
panchakarma.caution: Panchakarma is not suitable for everyone, including some people who are pregnant, very weak, or have certain medical conditions. It should only be done after a consultation.

faq.a: The duration depends on the person and the plan. The doctor will explain this at your consultation.
That depends on your age, health and medicines. Please speak with the doctor before booking.

faq.q: Will I need to change my diet?
faq.a: Yes, usually a light diet is advised before and after the programme. The doctor will guide you.

varmatherapy.lead: Varmam is a branch of the Siddha tradition of Tamil Nadu that works with vital points (varma points) of the body.
varmatherapy.overview: Varma therapy is closely related to the ancient Tamil martial art varma kalai. Practitioners apply gentle, skilled pressure and manipulation to specific points. Traditionally it is used to support movement, comfort and relaxation.
classes: Padu varmam: points affected by injury
Thodu varmam: points worked by touch
Thattu varmam: points worked by taps
Thaduvu varmam: points worked by massage
varmatherapy.classesNote: Classical texts describe 12 padu varmam and 96 thodu varmam points as the most widely used.
benefits: Traditionally used to support comfort and mobility
Often combined with oils, herbal preparations and exercises
Planned after a consultation so that it suits your condition
varmatherapy.caution: Varma therapy is a skilled hands-on practice and should only be received from a trained practitioner after assessment.

yoga.lead: Yoga and Ayurveda come from the same Vedic tradition and are traditionally practised together.

sections.heading: Yoga as a practice of attention
sections.body: Dharana (focus), dhyana (reflective meditation) and samadhi (absorption) are the inner limbs of yoga described in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras.

sections.heading: Yoga alongside Ayurvedic care
sections.body: Many people find that gentle postures, breathing practices (pranayama) and meditation fit well with an Ayurvedic routine.

sections.heading: Guidance for you
sections.body: We suggest practices suited to your age, strength and health, and we recommend asking the doctor first if you have a medical condition.

yoga.caution: Not every posture suits every body. Please speak with the doctor before starting if you are pregnant, recovering from surgery or have a medical condition.

organic.lead: In Ayurveda, food is the first form of care. Choosing fresh, minimally processed food is a good place to start.

sections.heading: What 'organic' means
sections.body: Organic usually refers to food grown without synthetic pesticides and fertilisers. Rules differ between countries, so look for recognised certification.

sections.heading: What it may offer
sections.body: Organic produce generally has fewer pesticide residues and is often fresher. Evidence for nutritional differences is mixed, so we avoid promising health outcomes.

sections.heading: Ayurvedic perspective
sections.body: Ayurveda pays attention to freshness, season, cooking method and eating according to appetite. The doctor can give you individual advice.

elakizhi.heading: Elakizhi (Ilakizhi)
elakizhi.body: Elakizhi is a traditional sudation therapy in which warm pouches of medicinal leaves are applied to the body. It is performed at the clinic under supervision.

offerings.lead: Our programmes are starting points. After a consultation the doctor adapts each one to you. Each tab has its own address you can share.

tabs.title: Panchakarma
tabs.summary: A supervised five-part cleansing and rejuvenation programme, planned individually.
tabs.body: Panchakarma is often preceded by oil massage and sudation, and followed by a light diet. See our Panchakarma page for details.

tabs.summary: Gentle therapies and routines traditionally used to support relaxation.
tabs.body: May include Shirodhara (a thin stream of warm oil on the forehead), Abhyanga (oil massage), Pizhichil (warm oil bath) and Elakizhi (herbal leaf pouches), chosen after consultation.

tabs.title: Weight management
tabs.summary: Diet, movement and traditional therapies for a healthier routine.
tabs.body: May include herbal powder massage (Udwarthanam), Kadikizhi, diet planning and yoga. Results vary, and the doctor will discuss realistic goals with you.

tabs.title: Diabetes care support
tabs.summary: Diet, lifestyle and supportive therapies alongside your regular diabetes management.
tabs.body: Ayurveda describes many types of Madhumeha. Our programme is supportive only. Please continue your medicines and monitoring as advised by your doctor.

tabs.title: Cleansing and rejuvenation
tabs.summary: A seasonal programme for rest and renewal.
tabs.body: Combines gentle cleansing therapies, massage and diet, and rejuvenating (rasayana) herbs where the doctor judges appropriate.

tabs.title: Fertility care support
tabs.summary: Supportive diet, lifestyle and therapies for couples.
tabs.body: Offered as supportive care alongside modern medical evaluation; we do not promise outcomes.

tabs.title: Post-pregnancy care
tabs.summary: Gentle rest, massage and nourishing diet after childbirth.
tabs.body: Traditional postnatal care that may include oil massage and warm herbal preparations, after review by the doctor.

tabs.title: Herbal beauty
tabs.summary: Skin and hair care with natural preparations, chosen for your constitution.
tabs.body: May include herbal face and body treatments and diet advice. A patch test is advised before any new preparation.

faq.q: Do I need to consult the doctor before using a product?
faq.a: Yes. We ask every patient to speak with the doctor first, because suitability depends on your health, age and any medicines you take.

faq.q: Can I buy products on this website?
faq.a: You can add products to your cart, but there is no online payment. Send the cart to the doctor: he calls you, checks what suits you, and then you collect from the pharmacy.

faq.q: What happens when I send my cart?
faq.a: The doctor sees it on his screen, calls you at the time you chose, and records his advice. You can follow it on your tracking page.

faq.q: Is Ayurvedic care a replacement for my regular treatment?
faq.a: No. It is offered as supportive care. Please continue medicines prescribed by your doctor unless they advise otherwise.
